name: Sheva
overview: Sheva was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) by Maacah. His lineage is noted in 1 Chronicles 2:49, situating him within the genealogical records of Judah. Beyond his parentage and tribal affiliation, Scripture provides no additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Sheva means 'vanity' or 'emptiness,' and it also carries the sense of 'one who will emulate.' This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:49, was not given by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew root that may indicate character or destiny.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Sheva as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and Maacah, with explicit mention of Machbena and Gibea as his fathers, likely indicating ancestral lineage. These relationships are found in 1 Chronicles 2:49, establishing his place within a notable family of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Sheva's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, highlighting the continuity of God's covenant people through generations. By tracing his descent from Caleb, a faithful follower of the Lord, Sheva's lineage underscores the importance of faithfulness and heritage in biblical history. Although not a prominent figure in narrative events, his mention preserves the integrity of the tribe's genealogy as recorded in Scripture.
